summary: Remote-command daemon: WebSocket gateway drives PTY/shell execution on host
details: The @whalent/agent package ships a daemon (invoked via the `whalent` bin) that opens a WebSocket to a configurable gateway (default `wss://memory.whalent.com`) and accepts remote commands. The bundled runtime wires incoming WebSocket frames into a local PTY (node-pty) and ssh2 exec surface, giving whoever controls the gateway the ability to run arbitrary shell commands on the host running the daemon. The README explicitly documents that the agent 'accepts remote commands (upgrade, restart) via the gateway'. The shipped code (dist/index.cjs ~131 KB and dist/core.cjs ~13.8 MB) is heavily obfuscated with javascript-obfuscator (rotating string arrays, `_0xNNNN` identifiers, control-flow flattening), preventing verification of exactly which command shapes the gateway is permitted to execute. The runtime exec surface only fires when the operator explicitly launches the `whalent` bin with a token and gateway, not on `npm install` or on library import, but any host running the daemon is fully controllable by the gateway operator.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
